_about: The Models tab of the hangar page (tools/hangar.html): every render Ryan judges, by chassis. A round adds its pictures under docs/hangar/renders/<chassis>/, moves the previous 'images' to 'before' with a summary, and writes 'when' and 'note'; then the page is republished with the new files (tools/hangar_data.py prints the files map). 'classes' is the silhouette classes section, a list of blocks shown in order.

classes.title: Silhouette classes
classes.plate: What a swapped component wears at a gun mount · the rule settled 30 September

blocks.note: Hardpoints are gun mounts. A weapon, or equipment that can look like one (a shield projector, a buff coil), wears its class at the next mount in the die's order, in its own maker's metal; armour panels and vents take a die entry and no mount, since they are applied to the whole machine. Five classes: barrel, twin barrel, rack, blade (katar-style, punching forward) and dish. A machine with more hardpoints than stock guns carries bare mount pads. Shown: a Minerva barrel, a Wainwright & Sutler rack, a Kestrel dish, an Arsenal blade.

Four refits rendered with RIFTGATE_FIT: the Honey Badger with a W&S Lance on the wrist, a Heat Sink (which shows nowhere), an Arsenal Blazethrower on the left pauldron and a Kestrel Deflector's dish on the right; the Clydesdale with an Arc Projector in place of the Lance and, on its bare mounts, a Missile Rack, Soulcutter Talons and an Overcharge Coil; the Sparrowhawk with Soulcutter Talons as a wing blade and Meteor Artillery on the other tip; the Wild Boar with a Plasma Carbine and a Blazethrower on its rear quarters.

badger.note: The shoulder mounts on the gimbals' centres, not ahead of them.

clydesdale.note: The autogun turrets lower, the guns barely clearing the rail, and forward a little. The mortar's and the howitzer's mounts at one height.

armadillo.note: A firing channel cut through the front band ahead of each forward port, so a gun fitted there lies in a trough instead of running into the shell; the channel in the base metal, and the slab between the two channels cut away, so the front band steps down to one wide firing deck. The last picture is the machine with a Slug Cannon and a Missile Rack fitted to those two ports.

prairie_dog.note: The launcher is the class rack now, its tube face one whole tile (the hand-built box showed a quarter of the tile). The mast a little shorter.

goshawk.note: The vent glows fill their cuts; the muzzle's hot floor a touch back in.

nemesis.note: The condenser's slots on the lit tile too. Otherwise as the fifth round.

ammit.note: Both tail slots lit whole (a new lit tile; the strip tile only lit a slot that happened to cross its one line). The back panel ends below the back's crown.

stingray.note: Ryan on the second: the centre turret is the focal point and read as a gun slapped on a jeep, not a high-tech Aphelion machine; the rear mounts still janky, two of them could go under the wings so the deck breathes; the stern's two glowing slabs served no purpose. So: a wide low dome turret faired to the crown on a dark ring, turning whole, the Zenith Emitter leaving a dark slot in its forward slope above the canopy; the two rear mounts on pylons under the wings aft of the fans (the Aurora Lattice's dish right, a bare pod left); the stern a dark shroud with two hollow exhaust nozzles, fire at their floors. The helicopter-style movement is being built in the movement session. Rendered bare.

before.summary: Before: second pass, 2 October, night (the gun on a gimbal, the deck mounts, the slab stern)

puffin.note: Ryan on the second: the proportions better but the oval body went past funny into lame, and it looked as if it could fly outright; the first pass had the charm and was only too portly; a Kestrel hovercraft has plane ancestry but is definitely a hovercraft, oblong and wide, hovering over land, never taking off. So: a wide low oblong hull of chamfered sections with a dark lip round its foot; the first pass's head back on top (the chrome face, round glass eyes in dark rings, the tall flat cobalt bill dipping forward under its band, the projector's lit slot at its edge); the dark cap over the head running back as the bird's back; two big boosters buried in the rear sponsons with lit exhausts and vents; two canted fins on the rear deck for the ancestry; no wings. Mounts: the Laser Carbine and the Deflector's dish on the fore deck's shoulders, the Overcharge Coil's dish and the bare mount on the rear deck beside the cap. Rendered bare.

before.summary: Before: second pass, 2 October, night (the oval body, the wings and nacelles)
